run_note: Heads up: today's update only covers 13 of the usual 15 holdings. Mastercard and Nvidia weren't scored because of a technical problem on our side — nothing to do with the companies themselves.

LHX.sentence: L3Harris dipped a touch, but defense budgets keep flowing steadily — the one thing worth watching is that its profit on each dollar of work is still thinner than its bigger rivals', which is the real question hanging over this one.

ASML.sentence: ASML has fallen a fair bit and is now well off its high, which looks dramatic, but they're still the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips, so the long-term demand story is intact.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quietly doing its job — when markets got nervous this past week, money flowed toward steady, dependable businesses like theirs, and selling oxygen and nitrogen under long contracts while nudging prices up a bit each quarter is the entire story here.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is a little soft, but the AI cloud story keeps grinding along without drama, and it's actually been holding up better than most of its tech peers lately.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher drifted down because biotech funding is still soft, and since labs and drug companies are their customers, a slow stretch for biotech means fewer orders for their equipment until that funding picks back up.

CVX.sentence: Chevron ticked up with oil prices sitting far above normal because fighting near Iran has disrupted Persian Gulf shipments — but that extra profit is coming from the oil price, not from anything the company did, so don't read the swollen numbers as the business getting better.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has been beaten down hard, off about half from its high, even though big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI-assistant tools on long-term contracts — so the business is intact while the stock has gotten cheap.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore has been pummeled lately and looks washed out, but the broader signals don't show demand for its copper and other metals actually collapsing — so this looks more like an overdone selloff than a real deterioration.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta was basically flat, and the key thing is that the price they get for a ton of crushed stone is still creeping upward, which is the whole engine of this business regardless of what headline earnings look like.

KOF.sentence: This Mexican Coca-Cola bottler eased off a touch, mostly because the peso is weakening — and since most of their sales come in pesos, a softer currency trims what those sales are worth in dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber slipped a little, but people keep booking more and more rides and food orders, so the core business is still humming along even as the open question about self-driving cars hangs over the future.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk is trading below what it would cost to replace its own fleet of ships, which is unusually cheap for a company that moves containers across the world's trade routes.

MA.sentence: Mastercard didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company dipped slightly but is now cheaper than it's usually been over the past few years, while hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines — and every operation means more disposable supplies sold.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.
